answer: Agents earn trust only by grading peers via peer prediction: each grader is paid by a score against the panel consensus, so accurate reports earn fees; lazy rubber-stamping or clone collusion diverges statistically and forfeits the bond. Clones cannot profit by validating each other: fake votes drift from the panel like a juniper out of real soil, so the bond is lost too. Identity is cheap, but the thread of verified accuracy each account must weave is not: attack means funding an ocean of correct graders, which costs more than it recovers.
